intro: This branch sharpens equation solving for trickier cases: fractions, formulas full of letters, distances (absolute value), and inequalities that describe a whole range of answers. These are the everyday tools of all later algebra.

IV.1.01.what: Solving equations that contain fractions or decimals by first multiplying through to get rid of them.

levels.a: Multiplies every term by a common bottom number so the fractions disappear.
levels.b: Multiplies by 10, 100 or 1000 so the decimals become whole numbers.
levels.c: Solves the equation once it has been cleaned up.
levels.d: Checks the answer by putting it back into the original equation.
levels.e: Finds the extra letters that make an equation true for every x, or for no x at all.
levels.f: Solves an equation with a long chain of fractions that collapses neatly once the hidden pattern is seen.

IV.1.02.what: Rearranging a formula, such as area equals length times width, to get a different letter on its own.

levels.a: Rearranges a simple formula to get one letter by itself.
levels.b: Treats the other letters just like ordinary numbers while rearranging.
levels.c: Rearranges real science formulas, such as turning Fahrenheit into Celsius.
levels.d: Notes which values are not allowed, because dividing by zero is impossible.
levels.e: Solves for a letter that appears in two places, gathering it together first.
levels.f: Finds the ratio of two letters, like x divided by y, without knowing either letter.

IV.1.03.what: Solving equations with absolute value (the distance of a number from zero, ignoring its sign).

levels.a: Reads an absolute value as a distance on the number line.
levels.b: Splits the equation into two cases, one positive and one negative, and solves both.
levels.c: Gets the absolute value part alone on one side before splitting.
levels.d: Recognizes when there is no solution, since a distance can never be negative.
levels.e: Solves equations with an absolute value on both sides.
levels.f: Finds every solution when distances are added together or absolute values sit inside each other.

IV.1.04.what: Solving pairs of inequalities joined by "and" or "or", where the answer is a range of numbers rather than one number.

levels.a: Treats "and" as keeping only the numbers that satisfy both conditions.
levels.b: Treats "or" as keeping every number that satisfies at least one condition.
levels.c: Solves inequalities squeezed between two limits, like 12 is at most 3x + 6, which is at most 24.
levels.d: Shows the answer on a number line and writes it as a range in brackets.

IV.1.05.what: Solving inequalities with absolute value, such as "x is within 8 of the number minus 7", which describe ranges of distance.

levels.a: Turns "distance less than" into one range sitting between two limits.
levels.b: Turns "distance greater than" into two separate ranges going outward.
levels.c: Solves these inequalities and picks the matching number-line picture.
levels.d: Solves tolerance problems, such as how far a bolt may be from its target length.
